title: Police report finds shooting of Adam Brian Purdie justified
article: Adam Brian Purdie, 28, was shot after he tried to speed away from an officer who had spotted an assault rifle in Purdie's car earlier this year in Surrey.
The shooting was investigated by the Saanich Police Department, which has ruled the officer was justified in firing 30 rounds to protect himself.
The report, released on Wednesday, paints a picture of Purdie the night he died. It contends he was armed with a rifle, high on drugs, and possibly heading to his ex-girlfriend's home.
It was March 2nd when Purdie was pulled over by the RCMP after an officer saw the rifle.

Purdie took off and was stopped 15 minutes later at an intersection where police had deployed a spike belt. A cruiser was used to take Purdie's car off the road, and that's when the gun fight started, between the officer in his car on the right, and Purdie still at the wheel of his car on the left.
It wasn't clear at the time, but has since been determined, Purdie also shot back.
The unnamed officer, a seven-year veteran of the force, fired 30 rounds into Purdie's vehicle, killing him with a wound to his upper body.
The external investigation looked at Purdie's computer, Blackberry, and interviewed 80 people. The Saanich police found that the officer who opened fire that night may have saved several lives.
